A shed is one plane over the whole 7.5 m of this plan where a gable climbs half of it, so across the 441 plans C1's own footprint band allows, 231 of them cannot reach the 15-20 ft ridge band the same family authors — at any eave in its 9-11 ft band and at any pitch between 22.6 and 36.9 degrees. This building's own plan is not one of them; the C1 family is refused as a whole rather than plan by plan.

The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.
